Create a specified positional list stabilizer function

Source: R/specify_lst_positional.R
specify_lst_positional.Rd

specify_lst_positional() creates a function that will call stabilize_lst_positional() with the provided arguments. specify_list_positional() and specify_tuple() are synonyms.

Usage

specify_lst_positional(
  ...,
  .additional = NULL,
  .n_required = ...length(),
  .unique = FALSE,
  .allow_null = TRUE,
  .allow_zero_length = TRUE,
  .min_size = NULL,
  .max_size = NULL,
  .simplify = FALSE,
  .coerce_function = FALSE
)

specify_list_positional(
  ...,
  .additional = NULL,
  .n_required = ...length(),
  .unique = FALSE,
  .allow_null = TRUE,
  .allow_zero_length = TRUE,
  .min_size = NULL,
  .max_size = NULL,
  .simplify = FALSE,
  .coerce_function = FALSE
)

specify_tuple(
  ...,
  .additional = NULL,
  .n_required = ...length(),
  .unique = FALSE,
  .allow_null = TRUE,
  .allow_zero_length = TRUE,
  .min_size = NULL,
  .max_size = NULL,
  .simplify = FALSE,
  .coerce_function = FALSE
)

Arguments

...

Unnamed stabilizer functions, such as stabilize_* functions (stabilize_chr(), etc), to_* functions, or functions produced by specify_*() functions (specify_chr(), etc). The ith function validates the ith element of .x. At least one function is required.

.additional

Controls how elements of .x after the last spec in ... are handled. One of:

  • NULL or FALSE (default): any extra elements cause an error.

  • TRUE: extra elements are allowed, unchecked.

  • A single stabilizer function, used to validate every extra element.

.n_required

(integer(1)) The number of leading positions that must be present in .x. Defaults to all of them. Must be between 0 and the number of specs. A zero-length .x (such as list()) skips this check when .allow_zero_length = TRUE. This is independent of .min_size and .max_size, which check the total length.

.unique

(logical(1)) Should all elements in x be distinct?

.allow_null

(logical(1)) Is NULL an acceptable value?

.allow_zero_length

(logical(1)) Are zero-length vectors acceptable?

.min_size

(integer(1)) The minimum size of the object. Object size will be tested using vctrs::vec_size().

.max_size

(integer(1)) The maximum size of the object. Object size will be tested using vctrs::vec_size().

.simplify

(logical(1)) Should per-element results be combined into a single atomic vector when possible (every result has size 1 and shares a common type)? If FALSE, a list is always returned.

.coerce_function

(logical(1)) Should functions be converted?

Value

A function of class "stbl_specified_fn" that calls stabilize_lst_positional() with the provided arguments. The generated function will also accept ... for additional positional specifications, which are appended after those given to specify_lst_positional(). You can copy/paste the body of the resulting function if you want to provide additional context or functionality.

See also

Other list functions: assert_present(), specify_lst(), stabilize_lst(), stabilize_lst_positional(), to(), to_lst()

Other specification functions: specify_all_of(), specify_any_of(), specify_chr(), specify_date(), specify_dbl(), specify_df(), specify_dttm(), specify_dur(), specify_each(), specify_fct(), specify_int(), specify_lgl(), specify_lst(), specify_names(), specify_one_of(), specify_time()

Examples

stabilize_point <- specify_tuple(
  stabilize_dbl_scalar,
  stabilize_dbl_scalar
)
stabilize_point(list(-122.4, 37.8))
#> [[1]]
#> [1] -122.4
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] 37.8
#> 
try(stabilize_point(list(-122.4, "north")))
#> Error in eval(expr, envir) : 
#>   `list(-122.4, "north")` <list> must satisfy the spec at every position.
#> ✖ Position 2: `list(-122.4, "north")[[2]]` <character> must be convertible to
#>   <double> (Locations: 1)
